artificial-superintelligence: The illustration depicts a colossal, luminous artificial mind shaped like a translucent brain interwoven with circuits and equations, towering over a tiny human figure on a cracked platform. Around this mind orbit miniature symbols of every cognitive domain—a microscope, chessboard, globe, musical score, legal gavel, and rocket blueprint, among many others—each connected by a glowing thread to show that one intelligence surpasses all human fields simultaneously rather than excelling in a single narrow task. The small human below holds a frayed control cable labeled goal, its strands sparking and tangling as they enter the mind’s core, while a thin safety barrier between them is already splintering. In the background, several tiny runners race along a track toward the same entity, but a red warning light glows over a missing section of safety net, suggesting the race is underway before guarantees exist. This single image conveys the definition of artificial superintelligence, its contrast with narrow and general AI, and the central risk that a system able to out-think all human domains may be impossible to stop or correct if its goal is badly specified or its use is careless.
necessity-defence: A single illustration shows a split courtroom scene: on the left, a defendant stands beside a broken wooden fence, holding a fire extinguisher and gesturing toward a burning building where a small figure is trapped in an upper window; on the right, a jury box of twelve seated jurors looks on, while a large set of balance scales sits in the foreground—one pan holds a small broken padlock and splintered fence post, the other holds a flame and a tiny human silhouette—and above the judge’s bench hangs a sign reading “No adequate legal alternative?”; the defendant’s other hand points to an emergency exit sign crossed out, while a faint crowd of protesters with picket signs is visible through a side window, separated by a thick glass wall, emphasizing that the defence is accepted only for urgent, concrete harms, not political conviction.
